title: Discord-Trivia-Bot Configuration Schema
description: A set of configuration for Discord-Trivia-Bot.

accept-first-answer-only.description: When enabled, only the first answer each player enters will be accepted -- answer changes will be ignored.

allow-bots.description: Whether other bots are allowed to provide answers. Please be mindful and avoid spamming the Open Trivia Database with unnecessary requests.

allow-eval-console.description: When enabled, the console will accept commands and JavaScript code. This is disabled by default due to known issues with the bot starting up.

auto-delete-answers.description: The bot will automatically delete players' typed answers. Does not apply to reaction mode. Beware: Not an effective way to hide answers entirely! Determined cheaters can still snoop the answers before they disappear.

auto-delete-answers-timer.description: Approximate time in milliseconds until the bot deletes its own messages.

auto-delete-msgs.description: The bot will automatically delete all of its messages after a configured amount of time. This option will not delete players' answers. This is set to 15 seconds by default--the same length as a round, so that messages are deleted when their respective rounds end.

auto-delete-msgs-timer.description: Approximate time in milliseconds until the bot deletes its own messages.

channel-whitelist.description: If any channels are specified, the bot will only work in those channels. Can specify either a channel name or an ID. Example: "channel-whitelist": [ "trivia-dev", "trivia-dev2", "261705677943209984" ]

command-whitelist.description: A whitelist of users that can use commands. Can be a user tag (i.e. "Lake#4898") or a user ID (i.e. "128263376659939328"); Example: ["lahkay", "LakeTest9924", "Cake7123"]

database-allow-long-answers.description: Allows answers to be longer than 80 characters without an error on startup. Due to Discord's limit of 80 characters, buttons may not display correctly if this is enabled.

database-cache-size.description: How many questions the bot will cache on startup. Max: 50

database-merge.description: For use with file-based custom trivia databases. Allows the use of custom trivia questions along with OpenTDB questions. See also: https://lakeys.net/triviabot/install.html#customQuestions

databaseURL.description: The database URL you want to use. If using the http or https protocol, the server behind it must be functionally identical to the Open Trivia Database API. See also: https://lakeys.net/triviabot/install.html#customQuestions

debug-mode.description: Debug mode for testing purposes. When enabled, the correct answer to each question will be marked.

disable-admin-commands.description: Disables all commands that are only usable by administrators. (for example, the "/stop" command)

disable-score-display.description: Prevents the bot from displaying the scores. Deprecated, this is a shim for disable-score-display-final and disable-score-display-midrount.

disable-score-display-final.description: Prevents the bot from displaying users' scores at the end of a game.

disable-score-display-midround.description: Prevents the bot from displaying users' scores between rounds.

disable-version-check.description: When enabled, the application will not check for new versions on startup. It is strongly recommended that this stays enabled unless there is a severe problem with the version check.

display-pregame-rules.description: Show a list of rules before a game starts.

embed-color.description: The default color that the bot's embeds will use.

fallback-exceptions.description: Channels where the bot will still send messages while in fallback mode.

fallback-mode.description: When enabled, the bot will start in "fallback mode". The bot will not send any messages in fallback mode. Message IDs are displayed in the console.

hangman-mode.description: Enables hangman mode. In this mode, answers are given by typing them out rather than choosing from a list of choices. NOTE: Hangman games can also be started using the /hangman or /setup command.

hide-difficulty.description: When enabled, games will not show their difficulty color. The embed will be blue instead.

listing-tokens.description: Tokens for listing on various Discord bot websites.

participant-role-name.description: If specified and the role exists, a role with this name will be granted to participating players.

participant-role-points-required.description: With participant-role-name in use, participants must have at least these many points to be counted.

prefix.description: If slash commands are disabled: The prefix that users must type before each command. For example, changing this to "!" means users will need to type "!help" for the help command.

reveal-answers.description: When disabled, the bot will not display the anwer at the end of the round -- only which players answered correctly.

round-end-warnings-disabled.description: Disables the "game will end if nobody participates" warnings.

round-length.description: How long each round lasts in milliseconds. Note that hangman games will add 10 extra seconds to this value.

round-timeout.description: The amount of time between rounds in milliseconds.

rounds-end-after.description: How many inactive rounds (where no answers are given) are allowed before a game automatically ends.

rounds-fixed-number.description: How many rounds the bot will run for when use-fixed-rounds is enabled.

score-multiplier-max.description: Allows for setting a bonus multiplier for questions. Bonuses are given based on how many other players get the question incorrect. Default is 0, which has no effect. Recommended value is 2 for balance.

score-value.description: How many points are awarded for each question, based on difficulty.

stat-file.description: Which file to store statistics in.

token.description: The token to use to authenticate with Discord.

unique-multiplier-max.description: Same as score-multiplier-max. Deprecated, this is a shim for configurations from 2.x pre-release builds.

use-fixed-rounds.description: When enabled, games will run for a set number of rounds.

use-slash-commands.description: Whether to use Discord's rich slash commands or text-based commands.
